utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we proceed, could I have an indication that both the accused can understand what is being said. It is enough if you give me, both of you, a nod, to acknowledge that you are receiving what I am saying in a language that you can understand. Thumbs up from you. And a nod from you. I'm satisfied. Thank you. Could we then have the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mark Harmon on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. Appearing with me, Carmela Javier, who is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alan Yatvin, of Philadelphia, representing Milan Lukic, and with me is co-counsel Jelena Lopicic-Jancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Djuro Cepic, Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic on my left-hand side. With me, Jens Dieckmann is a co-counsel and Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: As you know, this is the first Status Conference that I am, as Pre-trial Judge, chairing. This case has obviously been characterised by the fact that we have a parallel proceeding going on in the shape and form of an 11 bis referral. And it is -- I would like to say that up front that it is a bit unfortunate that this happens in circumstances where the Referral Bench is handing down its decision without too much delay, problems should not normally occur. I am not saying this in order to indicate that I am criticising another arm, as it were, of the Tribunal, but I merely note that the 11 bis proceedings have been ongoing since February last year. There was a meeting on the 15th of September, also last year, where the parties put forward their arguments, and now the Referral Bench have been considering the issue and no decision has been announced as of yet. Again, I'm not privy, obviously, to what the other Chamber is doing. Now, as a decision by me, a day before the oral arguments in the Referral Bench issue, or the 11 bis issue, was called, and that was in order to obviously in anticipation of a swift decision by the Referral Bench to suspend normal pre-trial proceedings. And I am certain that counsel is aware of that decision. The more so, since this was challenged by I think Mr. Yatvin. No, sorry, I'm wrong, it's Mr. Sredoje Lukic who challenged the decision, and certification was denied. That's where we are at this moment. I understood from the report which the senior legal officer gave me late yesterday about what transpired at the 65 ter conference that both accused now would like to see the order of suspension lifted and that has to do with the fact that both counsel expressed concern of the fact that they are not able to what they see as a job in the lack of discovery from the Prosecution. The Prosecution on its hand, and I'm saying this in order to facilitate the discussions, so I'm summarising where I think we are, and then I will allow you to comment on it. The Prosecution quotes, obviously, the need to not do what could be perceived to be unnecessary work, i.e., were it to transpire that the case is referred, any work in a pre-trial trial phase could be seen to be redundant. And obviously there is merit to that position, given the fact that, were it not for the fact that we have this parallel procedure, we would now a long time ago would have had a work plan and proceeded to implement that plan, starting obviously with the disclosure, which the Rules 66 and 65 dictate. And we would probably have times for marking down when pre-trial briefs from both sides should be submitted, and so on. Would it, I Pat here just to give the parties an indication. Would that be a fair assessment of what we are at this point? I give the floor first to the Prosecution. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, we're quite satisfied with that summary, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Yatvin -- is that how to proceed, protocol-wise? Mr. Yatvin first.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, quite succinctly put, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I also can say that is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, when I then understood that yesterday the issue of disclosure was raised again, I thought it proper, in order to save everybody's time, to proceed -- to see whether indeed things have changed since the 14th of September. From my perspective, at this point, time has obviously been a factor. It's five months now since the order to suspend the pre-trial proceeding. In order to assess whether time in itself is enough to change that, and to see when -- whether there could from now and in the foreseeable future be any indications from the Referral Bench when they're ready to hand down the decision. I have ordered, as you have seen, this morning that counsel for the two accused are to submit in writing the reasons for the motion to reconsider the suspension of the pre-trial proceedings. You have seven days in which to do that. Likewise, the Prosecution has seven days within which to respond to this. Any questions in relation to this order? Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, there are none, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Not a question, but as a technical matter, I should advise the Court that the motion was filed by Mr. Cepic, and because of the timing of the order I did not join at that point. I have discussed with Mr. Harmon rather than filing a completely separate motion, I would just join the original motion. And I will do that in writing and then we will probably file a joint motion on the reasons to keep this as consolidated as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Yatvin. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No questions about this issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm glad that you, Mr. Yatvin, clarified the technicalities surrounding this. We are always very much helped to have a joint motion from both of the accused. And I think from that perspective there is no reason, as far as I can see, to dwell on any other points that would follow from a pre-trial discussion. Maybe the smoke has lifted as far as was happening, as I have indicated in the Referral Bench, once we have the submissions on this particular issue, whether the order of 14 September, 2006 should be reconsidered; that is 14 days from now. With that, I ask whether the parties have anything else to raise during this Status Conference. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, not on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On behalf of the accused. Mr. Yatvin.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the issue of disclosure and the issues that flow from it are really our principal reason for having requested a Status Conference in the first place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I will also formally inquire as to whether the accused have any issues they would like to raise, since this is an opportunity for them, with or without the help of counsel. A shaking of a head would be fine. Two shakes of a head. Thank you very much. With that, I think that we have come to a close and I declare this conference adjourned. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.11 p.m.
